question: Under the tire problems section, what minimum tread depth does the manual require for front tires versus other tires?
choice_a: 4/32-inch on front tires, 2/32-inch on other tires
choice_b: 2/32-inch on front tires, 4/32-inch on other tires
choice_c: 6/32-inch on all tires equally
choice_d: 1/32-inch on front tires, 3/32-inch on other tires
explanation: The manual states you need at least 4/32-inch tread depth in every major groove on front tires, and 2/32-inch on other tires, with no fabric showing through the tread or sidewall.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 15

question: During a wheel and rim inspection, what does rust around the wheel nuts most likely indicate?
choice_a: The rim was recently repaired by welding
choice_b: The tire is a mismatched size
choice_c: The nuts may be loose, and tightness should be checked
choice_d: The wheel bearing seal is leaking
explanation: The manual notes that rust around wheel nuts may mean the nuts are loose, and instructs drivers to check tightness, then re-check after a tire has been changed.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 16

question: How much steering wheel play does the manual identify as enough to make a vehicle hard to steer?
choice_a: Any play greater than zero degrees
choice_b: More than 10 degrees, about 2 inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch wheel
choice_c: More than 45 degrees, about an eighth turn
choice_d: More than 90 degrees, a quarter turn of the wheel
explanation: The manual lists steering wheel play of more than 10 degrees, approximately 2 inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch steering wheel, as something that can make a vehicle hard to steer.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 16

question: Under suspension system defects, what happens to a vehicle if one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring?
choice_a: It is placed "out of service"
choice_b: It may keep running until the next scheduled maintenance
choice_c: It only needs a note in the trip log
choice_d: It is allowed to continue if the load is under half capacity
explanation: The manual states missing or broken leaves in a leaf spring can be dangerous, and if one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle will be put "out of service," though any defect could be dangerous.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 16

question: What emergency warning devices does the manual say vehicles must carry for parked vehicles?
choice_a: Three reflective triangles, or at least 6 fusees, or 3 liquid burning flares
choice_b: One reflective triangle and a flashlight
choice_c: A single road flare and a whistle
choice_d: Two orange cones and a warning sign
explanation: The manual lists warning devices for parked vehicles as three reflective triangles, or at least 6 fusees, or 3 liquid burning flares, alongside a fire extinguisher and spare electrical fuses.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 17

question: After starting the engine, what does it mean if the ABS indicator light on the dash comes on and then stays on instead of turning off?
choice_a: The parking brake has not fully released
choice_b: The transmission fluid level is low
choice_c: The oil pressure gauge needs recalibration
choice_d: The Anti-lock Braking System is not working properly
explanation: The manual states the ABS dash light should come on and then turn off; if it stays on, the ABS is not working properly (and for trailers, a yellow light staying on at the left rear means the same).
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 18

question: When checking gauges after starting the engine, air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within what time, and to about what governor cut-out range?
choice_a: Within 3 minutes, to a governor cut-out usually around 120-140 psi
choice_b: Within 30 seconds, to a governor cut-out usually around 60-80 psi
choice_c: Within 10 minutes, to a governor cut-out usually around 200 psi
choice_d: Within 1 minute, to a governor cut-out usually around 100 psi
explanation: The manual states air pressure should build from 50 to 90 psi within 3 minutes, continuing to a governor cut-out usually around 120-140 psi, and drivers should know their vehicle's specific requirements.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 18

question: In Step 7 of the inspection method, how do you test a vehicle with hydraulic brakes for leaks?
choice_a: Pump the brake pedal three times, then apply firm pressure and hold for five seconds; the pedal should not move
choice_b: Tap the brake pedal once and listen for a hissing sound
choice_c: Hold the brake pedal down for one full minute while idling
choice_d: Release the parking brake and coast to see if the vehicle drifts
explanation: The manual instructs pumping the brake pedal three times, then applying firm pressure and holding it for five seconds with the vehicle running; if the pedal moves, there may be a leak or other problem that must be fixed before driving.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 21

question: How often must drivers of trucks and truck-tractors transporting cargo inspect the cargo's securement after the trip begins?
choice_a: Within the first 50 miles, then every 150 miles or every three hours, whichever comes first
choice_b: Only once, at the very start of the trip
choice_c: Every 500 miles regardless of time elapsed
choice_d: Once per day, at the end-of-day inspection only
explanation: The manual states drivers of trucks and truck-tractors transporting cargo must inspect the securement of the cargo within the first 50 miles of a trip and every 150 miles or every three hours after, whichever comes first.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 21

question: On a manual-transmission vehicle, what does the manual advise to avoid rolling back when starting from a stop?
choice_a: Fully release the clutch before touching the accelerator
choice_b: Partly engage the clutch before taking your right foot off the brake
choice_c: Shift directly into the highest available gear
choice_d: Rev the engine to redline before releasing the brake
explanation: The manual advises partly engaging the clutch before taking your right foot off the brake, and applying the parking brake when necessary to keep from rolling back into someone behind you.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 22

question: How does the manual say a driver should hold the steering wheel?
choice_a: Loosely, so it can self-correct after a bump
choice_b: With one hand, keeping the other free for controls
choice_c: Firmly, with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel
choice_d: With both hands stacked at the top center of the wheel
explanation: The manual instructs holding the wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides, since hitting a curb or pothole could otherwise pull the wheel away from an unprepared driver's hands.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 22

question: Why does the manual recommend backing and turning toward the driver's side whenever possible, even if it means going around the block?
choice_a: It lets the driver watch the rear of the vehicle out the side window, unlike backing toward the right
choice_b: State law requires driver-side backing in every case
choice_c: It reduces wear on the right-side tires
choice_d: It keeps exhaust fumes away from nearby pedestrians
explanation: The manual explains that backing toward the driver's side lets you watch the rear of the vehicle by looking out the side window, while backing toward the right side is very dangerous because you can't see as well.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 22

question: Per the manual, which type of manual transmission requires double clutching to change gears?
choice_a: Synchronized manual transmissions only
choice_b: Neither type requires double clutching on heavy vehicles
choice_c: Both types require it equally
choice_d: Most heavy vehicles with unsynchronized manual transmissions; it is NOT required on a synchronized transmission
explanation: The manual states that most heavy vehicles with unsynchronized manual transmissions require double clutching to change gears, while double clutching is NOT required if the vehicle has a synchronized manual transmission.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 22

question: Why does the manual say a driver should slow down and downshift before starting down a hill?
choice_a: So the transmission can be left in neutral for the whole descent
choice_b: So the vehicle can be controlled without using the brakes hard, since overheated brakes can lose their braking power
choice_c: So the driver can briefly take both hands off the wheel
choice_d: So fuel consumption is minimized on the way down
explanation: The manual explains that downshifting before a hill lets a driver control speed without using the brakes hard, because overheating the brakes can cause them to lose their braking power.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 23

question: What benefit does the manual give for downshifting to the right gear before entering a curve, rather than after?
choice_a: It lets the driver use some power through the curve to help the vehicle stay stable, and allows speeding up once out of the curve
choice_b: It prevents the transmission from overheating in hot weather
choice_c: It is only useful for automatic transmissions
choice_d: It allows the driver to skip using the steering wheel through the curve
explanation: The manual states that downshifting before entering a curve lets the driver use some power through the curve to help the vehicle stay more stable while turning, and also allows speeding up once out of the curve.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 23

question: The manual describes four basic types of retarders. When does it say a retarder should be turned off?
choice_a: Only when the vehicle is unloaded
choice_b: Whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow covered, because it may cause the drive wheels to skid
choice_c: Only when driving above 55 mph
choice_d: Retarders should never be turned off once engaged
explanation: The manual describes four basic types of retarders (exhaust, engine, hydraulic, electric) and cautions that when drive wheels have poor traction, the retarder may cause them to skid, so it should be turned off on wet, icy, or snow-covered roads.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 23

question: The manual says most good drivers look how far ahead of their vehicle while driving?
choice_a: About 2 to 3 seconds ahead
choice_b: At least 12 to 15 seconds ahead
choice_c: Only as far as the next intersection
choice_d: At least one full minute ahead at all speeds
explanation: The manual states most good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead, which is about one block at lower speeds or about a quarter mile at highway speeds.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 24

question: When can mirror adjustment be checked accurately on a combination vehicle, according to the manual?
choice_a: Only when the trailer(s) are straight
choice_b: Only while the vehicle is backing up
choice_c: Only after the engine has idled for 15 minutes
choice_d: Only at night with headlights on
explanation: The manual states mirror adjustment should be checked prior to the start of any trip and can only be checked accurately when the trailer(s) are straight.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 24

question: During a lane change, what should a driver check for right after signaling, according to the manual's mirror-check sequence?
choice_a: That the fuel gauge shows enough fuel to complete the maneuver
choice_b: That the four-way flashers are switched off
choice_c: That no one has moved into the driver's blind spot
choice_d: That the trailer brake hand valve is released
explanation: The manual's lane-change mirror checks include checking mirrors right after signaling to make sure no one has moved into the blind spot, in addition to checks before, during, and after the lane change.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 24

question: How do curved (convex) mirrors change the way objects appear, according to the manual?
choice_a: Objects appear upside down
choice_b: Objects appear at the same size and distance as in a flat mirror
choice_c: Objects appear larger and closer than they really are
choice_d: Objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are
explanation: The manual explains that everything appears smaller in a convex mirror than it would look directly, and things also seem farther away than they really are, so drivers must allow for this.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 25

question: The manual gives three rules for using turn signals. What are they?
choice_a: Signal only for left turns, honk while turning, and cancel immediately
choice_b: Signal early, signal continuously, and cancel the signal after completing the turn
choice_c: Signal after beginning the turn, signal intermittently, and cancel before turning
choice_d: Signal only in heavy traffic and leave it on afterward
explanation: The manual's three rules for turn signals are: signal early (well before turning), signal continuously (don't cancel until the turn is complete), and cancel the signal after the turn.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 26

question: When it is legal, what does the manual suggest doing before passing a pedestrian or bicyclist who may not see you?
choice_a: Honk the horn continuously until fully past
choice_b: Swerve wide into the next lane without any warning
choice_c: Turn on the four-way emergency flashers and keep them on through the pass
choice_d: Tap the horn lightly, or at night flash your lights from low to high beam and back
explanation: The manual advises tapping the horn lightly, or at night flashing your lights from low to high beam and back, when passing someone who may not see you, while still driving carefully in case they don't respond.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 26

question: If you must stop on or by a one-way or divided highway, at what distances should you place your warning devices toward the approaching traffic?
choice_a: 5 feet, 50 feet, and 100 feet
choice_b: 50 feet, 250 feet, and 500 feet
choice_c: 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet
choice_d: 20 feet, 150 feet, and 300 feet
explanation: The manual states that on a one-way or divided highway, warning devices should be placed 10 feet, 100 feet, and 200 feet toward the approaching traffic.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 26

question: If you stop on a two-lane road carrying traffic in both directions, where does the manual say to place your warning devices?
choice_a: 300 feet behind and 300 feet ahead of the vehicle only
choice_b: Within 10 feet of the front or rear corners of the vehicle, and 100 feet behind and ahead of it
choice_c: Only 500 feet behind the vehicle
choice_d: Within 2 feet of the vehicle, no farther out
explanation: The manual states that on a two-lane road carrying traffic in both directions, warning devices go within 10 feet of the front or rear corners to mark the vehicle's location, plus 100 feet behind and ahead of it.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 26

question: On a wet road, the manual's example says a driver should reduce speed by about how much?
choice_a: About one-tenth, for example slowing from 55 to about 50 mph
choice_b: No reduction is needed if the tires are new
choice_c: About one-third, for example slowing from 55 to about 35 mph
choice_d: About three-quarters, for example slowing from 55 to about 14 mph
explanation: The manual instructs reducing speed by about one-third on a wet road, using the example of slowing from 55 to about 35 mph, with even greater reductions on packed snow or ice.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 28

question: How slow can a vehicle be going and still hydroplane, according to the manual, if there is a lot of water on the road?
choice_a: As low as 30 mph
choice_b: Hydroplaning requires at least 75 mph
choice_c: Only above 65 mph
choice_d: Speed has no bearing on hydroplaning
explanation: The manual states hydroplaning can occur at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is a lot of water on the road, and is more likely with low tire pressure or worn tread.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 28

question: What rule of thumb does the manual give for following distance ahead of your vehicle at speeds below 40 mph?
choice_a: Two car lengths for every 10 mph of speed
choice_b: A flat 3 seconds regardless of vehicle length
choice_c: One second for each 50 feet of vehicle length
choice_d: At least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length, adding 1 more second above 40 mph
explanation: The manual's rule is at least one second of following distance for each 10 feet of vehicle length at speeds below 40 mph, adding 1 more second of following distance at speeds above 40 mph.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 30

question: If you notice you are being tailgated, what does the manual specifically advise against doing?
choice_a: Turning on your headlights and braking smoothly
choice_b: Increasing your following distance and signaling early
choice_c: Making quick changes in speed or direction, or speeding up
choice_d: Using your mirrors and slowing down gradually
explanation: The manual advises drivers who are tailgated to avoid quick changes in speed or direction and not to speed up, since it's safer to be tailgated at a low speed than a high one; instead, increasing following distance is recommended.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 30

question: According to the manual, why should drivers not assume the height posted at a bridge or overpass is accurate?
choice_a: Posted heights are only estimates and are updated annually
choice_b: Re-paving or packed snow may have reduced clearance since the height was posted
choice_c: Heights are always rounded up for a safety margin
choice_d: Bridge heights are only posted for cars, not trucks
explanation: The manual warns that re-paving or packed snow may have reduced clearances since the heights were posted, and also notes that an empty cargo van is higher than a loaded one, so clearing a bridge while loaded doesn't guarantee clearing it while empty.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 30

question: For a right turn that a truck or bus cannot make without swinging into another lane, what does the manual instruct?
choice_a: Swing wide to the left as you begin the turn to gain clearance
choice_b: Turn wide as you complete the turn, keeping the rear of the vehicle close to the curb
choice_c: Stop and back up until another driver waves you through
choice_d: Take the turn at normal speed to avoid blocking traffic
explanation: The manual instructs turning wide as you complete the turn while keeping the rear of the vehicle close to the curb, which stops other drivers from passing on the right; it warns against turning wide to the left at the start, since a following driver may try to pass on the right.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 31

question: On a left turn, what does the manual say you must do before starting the turn to avoid hitting another vehicle due to off-tracking?
choice_a: Make sure you have reached the center of the intersection first
choice_b: Begin turning as soon as you enter the intersection
choice_c: Signal continuously for at least 30 seconds beforehand
choice_d: Come to a complete stop in the middle of the intersection
explanation: The manual states that on a left turn, you must make sure you have reached the center of the intersection before you start the turn; turning too soon can cause the left side of your vehicle to hit another vehicle because of off-tracking.
source_note: Colorado CDL Manual (2023 CDL Testing System, DR 2251, June 2023), Colorado Department of Revenue - Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 2 - Driving Safely, p. 31
